raw_case_text:
A 63-year-old dark-skinned male patient, hypertensive, reported the appearance of erythematous-brown, edematous and itchy plaques on the abdomen in the beginning of 2013, with inconclusive histopathology and immunohistochemistry. He remained under follow-up and presented to the outpatient dermatology clinic in February 2015 with an ulcerated tumor on the skin of the nose and worsening of the previous lesions. On clinical examination, he had brown and edematous plaques on the frontal region, associated with alopecia of the eyebrows and hairline, in addition to a deforming tumor on the nose (Figure 1). ENT assessment demonstrated an infiltrative lesion, with total obstruction of the right nostril and partial of the left nostril, with associated mucoid discharge. No lesions on the palate or jugal mucosa were seen. Slightly lichenified brown plaques were seen on the upper and lower limbs, predominantly on the trunk and ulcerated tumors on the upper limbs (Figure 2).
There was no lymphadenopathy. The suspicion was of paracoccidioidomycosis, leishmaniasis, syphilis, leprosy, sarcoidosis, mycosis fungoides, and lethal midline granuloma. Blood samples were collected, and microscopy, Montenegro's test, tuberculin test, bacilloscopy, serology for hepatitis, HIV and syphilis were all performed, and all were negative. Chest radiograph and abdomen ultrasound were unremarkable. New biopsies were taken, with unspecific findings. The patient's follow-up was then irregular, with long intervals between appointments, with worsening of the tumor on the nose. In July 2015 three new biopsies from different skin lesions were taken and the histopathology of the abdominal plaque revealed a dense atypical mononuclear infiltrate, involving the remaining follicular sheath and eccrine glands associated to psoriasiform hyperplasia of the epidermis and granulomatous reaction (Figure 3). Immunohistochemistry favored the diagnostic interpretation of non-Hodgkin epidermotropic and folliculotropic T-cell cutaneous lymphoma, CD4 and CD30 positive (Figures 4 and 5). The patient was seen by the hematology team and chemotherapy with gemcitabine and interferon, associated to phototherapy were scheduled.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 63-year-old hypertensive male presented in February 2015 with a deforming, ulcerated nasal tumor and worsening pruritic erythematous-brown plaques and ulcerated tumors over his forehead, trunk, and extremities of 2 years' duration.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: In early 2013, the patient developed pruritic, edematous erythematous-brown plaques on his abdomen with inconclusive initial biopsies. Following irregular follow-up, he returned in February 2015 and July 2015 with progressive worsening of the truncal and limb lesions and a deforming, ulcerated tumor on his nose causing bilateral nasal obstruction and mucoid discharge.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for cutaneous pruritus, nasal obstruction, and mucoid nasal discharge.

objective.physical_examination: Cutaneous examination revealed edematous brown plaques on the forehead with eyebrow and anterior hairline alopecia, a deforming ulcerated tumor on the external nose, slightly lichenified brown plaques over the trunk and upper/lower extremities, and ulcerated tumors on the upper limbs, without palpable lymphadenopathy. Otolaryngological (ENT) examination showed an infiltrative endonasal mass causing total right nostril and partial left nostril obstruction with mucoid discharge, while the palate and buccal mucosa were spared.
objective.routine_investigations: Direct microscopy, slit-skin smear bacilloscopy, Montenegro skin test, tuberculin skin test, and serologies for hepatitis, HIV, and syphilis were all negative. Chest radiograph and abdominal ultrasound were normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Three repeat skin biopsies obtained in July 2015 (including from the abdominal plaque) demonstrated psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia, a granulomatous reaction, and a dense atypical mononuclear infiltrate with epidermotropism and infiltration of hair follicle sheaths (folliculotropism) and eccrine glands; immunohistochemistry was positive for CD4 and CD30.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Histopathology and immunohistochemistry confirmed CD4+, CD30+ epidermotropic and folliculotropic cutaneous T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (granulomatous/folliculotropic mycosis fungoides with large-cell transformation), ruling out leprosy, leishmaniasis, paracoccidioidomycosis, syphilis, sarcoidosis, and extranodal NK/T-cell nasal-type lymphoma. The patient was referred to hematology and scheduled for systemic chemotherapy with gemcitabine and interferon combined with phototherapy.
